claim_one_line: THE FINITE COVERS, SEALED AND RUNNING (9c28d076; the addendum beside the seal at eeb20c44; sL-10 item 16, sm:B1535's Corollary C3, second place): does sm:B1515's frame carry three generations on a connected finite cover of degree <= 12 of m004 (176) or m003 (148), or on their Q8 towers (m = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18), at any pulled-back character of finite order (8,148 and 35,100 characters, Lemma Z'') and any class of the cover (the pulled-back class at kappa^5 = 1; every cusp stratum at two classes wherever min(capW, capL2) >= 2)? Two routes sharing no linear algebra: N (the cover read on the base by Lemmas S' and O, FLINT, p < 2^24) and R (the cover's own Reidemeister-Schreier presentation, PARI, p < 2^31). Ten predictions sealed with priors summing to 7.88; NEGATIVE on three only if both routes read the whole population and P1, P2, P8 and P10 hold. The banked identity holds on the amended files; the four runs started at 06:40:05Z. No outcome has been read. 0 of 19.

sources.cite: A. Putman and B. Wieland, Abelian quotients of subgroups of the mapping class group and higher Prym representations, J. London Math. Soc. 88 (2013) 79-96, arXiv:1106.2747

sources.says: the higher Prym representations are conjectured to have no non-zero finite orbits for genus >= 2 (the paper notes it fails for genus 0 and 1); Appendix A: pi_1 of the once-punctured torus onto Q8 on a free basis gives a genus-3 cover with 4 punctures, V_K = Q^2 + H_Q, the mapping class group acting on H_Q through a finite group

sources.says: a lattice generated by two parabolics has PH^1(R^4_1) = 0 (after Kapovich), so the figure-eight's is 0; dim PH^1 = dim H^2 - t and dim H^1 = dim ker res + t; by Long (Bull. London Math. Soc. 1987, cited through them) some finite covers admit bending deformations
